body.heading: The puzzle
paragraphs: A man walks into a bar and asks the bartender for a glass of water. The bartender pulls out a gun and points it at him. The man pauses, says 'thank you', and walks out - without drinking anything. No shots are fired, no crime is involved, and both men behave perfectly sensibly. What is going on?

This is a lateral-thinking puzzle, a story that seems impossible because your brain quietly adds assumptions that were never stated. The standard way to solve one is to interrogate those assumptions with yes-or-no questions: Was the man thirsty? Was he in danger? Did he get what he came for? That last question is the key that turns the lock.

body.heading: The solution
paragraphs: The man had hiccups. He asked for water because drinking is a common hiccup cure. The bartender, recognising the problem, chose a faster remedy: a sudden fright. The shock cured the hiccups on the spot - so the man, no longer needing the water, thanked him and left. Every strange detail was a clue: the thanks only makes sense if the gun was a favour.

Notice how the solution works. Nothing in the story was false; the impossibility lived entirely in the listener's assumptions - that a gun means a threat, and that a man who asks for water must be thirsty. Lateral puzzles are exercises in finding the assumption you did not know you had made.

body.heading: Try it yourself
paragraphs: Two more, with the answers in the last lines of this section - cover them and think first. One: a woman pushes her car up to a hotel, hands the owner some money, and announces that she is bankrupt. Two: a man lives on the tenth floor; every morning he rides the lift to the ground floor, but coming home he rides only to the seventh and walks the rest - unless it is raining, when he rides all the way.

Answers: the woman is playing Monopoly - her token is the car, and the hotel is on a board square. The man is too short to reach the tenth-floor button; he can press the ground-floor button going down, and on rainy days he can press the tenth button with the tip of his umbrella.

takeaway: Lateral puzzles hide their answer behind an assumption - list what you are assuming, and the strange story turns ordinary.
